restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 so that beta = beta* in every trial, Y4 is held in the sub-class of 131,072 values of entry c66f230d's class, and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. Only outer steps that pass the exact filter of proof.md Section 8 are searched further: by Lemma F an outer step that fails it holds no trial with R = 0 and one of the seven E1 outcomes of beta*, so no counted success is lost; it passes 312,881,258,079 / 2^48 = 2^-9.8132 of uniform word pairs. Heuristic part: a search over 2^90.463 walked trials (2^69.463 outer steps of 2^21, drawn seven to a batch, one per 36-bit lane, independent: proof.md Lemma PL) for one whose remaining 128 chaining-value bits agree and that satisfies rule A succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under H1' and H4'.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) per unit, on a load/store machine with 64 registers and every constant an immediate operand (the cost model sets no register count); any other fetch of a memory word is a load, any write a store. A batch of seven outer steps, one per 36-bit lane, costs 640 units: step CO on packed words and both filter automata in every lane (525 counted), stored words, pass bitmap, dispatch. Only a passing lane is rebuilt on scalar words and runs the merged joint solver of proof.md 9.4 (at most 3 outcomes, 848 nodes, 96 leaves, 96 roots) and the certificate of each root: at most 144,640 units whatever its words. No sorting, no lookup by value, no table that grows with the trials. The algorithm halts with failure when more than CTR_PASS_BUDGET steps pass or after RUN_OUTER_STEPS steps; each row is charged at its budget (proof.md Sections 9, 11).

Randomized by eight fresh uniform 256-bit words per batch: lane i of the eight words gives the eight words of one outer step (proof.md Lemma PL). The success probability 0.39 holds only under heuristics H1' and H4'. The factor 99,033,509,302 in H1' is five sevenths of the model's conditional count, rounded down, and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments, which run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) because no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk's chaining value. The filter is exact; that the sampler's pass share equals 2^-9.8132 is measured, not proved, and enters only the pass budget (H4'). No full 2-round collision is exhibited or computed. The packed batch, the joint solver and the certificate are defined in proof.md; the submitted program contains and counts the outer step, the filter and the walk with its pass budget, one outer step at a time, and does not contain the batch, the solver or the certificate.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta, two bits of the sub-class, three 32-bit constants of the rule test, the beta* cube (beta*, mask, value) and the seven tau values and eps of the filter are stored in the program (92 bytes of advice). The constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by a participant's count; the sub-class and rule A were proposed by another AI model (GPT Sol 6.1) from exact counts that the participant's counter reproduces; beta* is the first of the 53 betas of the sub-class in an exhaustive ranking from the same counts, which also list its seven outcomes. preprocessing_log2 69.72 bounds the selection procedure of proof.md Section 12 in full and is included in time_log2: the search alone is below 2^68.751 units, the selection below 2^69.720. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the code, selection and search, all held at once (sum below 2^44). No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. Over the run's RUN_OUTER_STEPS independent uniform 256-bit words, let N_o be the number of listed good valid trials of one outer step (t != 0, R = 0, rule A, and an E1 outcome among the seven outcomes of beta*), counted over all of Q* whether or not the outer step passes the filter. (i) E[N_o] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = CTR_FACTOR * 2^-128, CTR_FACTOR = floor(5 * 138,646,913,024 / 7) = 99,033,509,302, about 2^-91.473 (just under five sevenths of the conditional model rate p of Lemma S1). (ii) The probability that no valid trial of the run is a listed good trial is at most exp(-0.49676) + 0.001. Given (i), rho = E[N_o(N_o-1)]/E[N_o] <= 0.0065 is sufficient for (ii) by Lemma S8. This is the premise of entry e7b17fd1 with the count restricted to the seven outcomes, which carry all of p, and with the factor at five sevenths of the count in place of one half. By Lemma F (exact) every listed good trial lies in an outer step that passes the filter, so N_o is zero on rejected outer steps (Lemma S9) and the rate per member of Q* of a passing outer step is q / pi_o, about 2^-81.660 if pi_o equals the exact share pi.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 in the sub-class of 131,072 values (Lemmas Q and Q2), E1.c1 drawn from the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 in every trial, t solved per trial and t = 0 skipped, outer words drawn from the run's fresh 256-bit words. Only outer steps that pass the exact filter of Section 8 are searched further; N_o counts all of Q* in every outer step.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model of Section 10, of the beta* part of the sub-class kept by rule A (seven outcomes, 67,698,688 = 1033 * 2^16; the counting program and its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1: conditioning the model on the cube does not bias the E3 side), taken at five sevenths, rounded down. The filter changes neither the count nor the premise: under the model all of p lies on passing outer steps (Lemma S9 (b)). Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: 2^45.6 real 32-bit counter trials whose measurable partial events match the exact model within about 1%; 2^43 real trials inside passing outer steps in which rule A and the E1 test keep their values over all outer steps and the listed E1 outcome is 0.979 +- 0.022 of its value; and a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted. The joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured at 32 bits.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 99,033,509,302 is assumed (five sevenths of the model count, rounded down). The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) of the same construction and measure neither the factor nor the counter half-collision, which no digest experiment can show. The transfer of the single-trial law to the actual sampler is partly proved (Lemmas S1-S9) and partly assumed in (i); the weak-dependence condition of (ii) is assumed, with a proved cap on the successes of one outer step (Section 10). Lemma F and Lemma S9 (a) use no law of the words; the 8-bit end-to-end run has no filter.

heuristics.statement: Supporting. With probability at least 0.9995 over the coins, at most CTR_PASS_BUDGET = 961,264,466,727,415,003 outer steps of a run pass the filter (about 2^59.738: RUN_OUTER_STEPS times the exact share pi = CTR_SHARE / 2^64 = 2^-9.8132, times 17/16), so the pass-count halt is not reached. Reaching it halts with failure; the time bound charges CTR_PASS_BUDGET passing outer steps.
heuristics.scope: The outer filter of proof.md Section 8 on the outer steps of step 1 of Section 9.1: the number of passing outer steps of a run, which is binomial with RUN_OUTER_STEPS independent steps and the sampler's pass probability pi_o (Lemma S9).
heuristics.extrapolation: pi is exact for independent uniform pairs (Y9, Y3 + Y4 + w8), with a certificate in Section 8. If pi_o <= 1.06 pi, the Chernoff bound puts more than CTR_PASS_BUDGET passing outer steps below exp(-2 * 10^12). Measured (Section 13, untrusted by the harness): 2^-9.8127 against 2^-9.8132 in a graphics-card run that kept 2^22.00 passing outer steps (z = +0.7); 74 of 65,536 real outer steps in the program's self-test (2^-9.791, z = +0.14).
heuristics.limitations: That pi_o equals pi, or is at most 1.06 pi, is not proved: the sampler's Y9 and Y3 + Y4 + w8 are not proved independent and uniform. The organizer does not run the self-test. The time bound and the exactness of the filter do not depend on pi_o.
